about: The Apostles’ Creed is the ancient baptismal symbol of the Church of Rome, traditionally arranged in twelve articles. In the first person it professes faith in God the Father, Jesus Christ, and the Holy Spirit, and then professes the Church, forgiveness of sins, resurrection of the body, and everlasting life. This recension retains a repeated Credo before the articles concerning the Holy Spirit.

seg.tr: I believe in God, the Father Almighty, Creator of heaven and earth;
and in Jesus Christ, His only Son, our Lord:

fn.w011: Begins the second complement governed by “Credo” (w001).
fn.w014: Apposition to the name and title “Iesum Christum”.
fn.w017: A further apposition to the name and title “Iesum Christum”.

seg.tr: who was conceived by the Holy Spirit, born of the Virgin Mary,

fn.w019: The relative pronoun refers to Jesus Christ in the preceding clause.
fn.w020: With “est” (w021), forms the perfect passive: “was conceived”.
fn.w025: A deponent participle sharing the understood “est” (w021).

seg.tr: suffered under Pontius Pilate, was crucified; died, and was buried.

fn.w029: A deponent participle with active meaning, sharing the understood “est” (w021).
fn.w032: The second part of the name “Póntio Piláto”.
fn.w034: The perfect participle of the deponent “morior”. With understood “est” (w021), it means “died”.

fn.w039: A plural noun after “ad”, denoting those below or their realm.

seg.tr: the third day He rose again from the dead;

fn.w041: Ablative of time. Feminine here, agreeing with “tértia” (w040).

fn.w047: The plural of “caelum”. In the plural it is masculine.

seg.tr: sits at the right hand of God the Father Almighty;
from thence He shall come to judge the living and the dead.

fn.w057: The infinitive states the purpose of the future coming.

seg.tr: I believe in the Holy Spirit,

fn.w061: The repeated verb opens the third group of articles in the selected devotional recension.

seg.tr: the Holy Catholic Church, the communion of Saints,
the forgiveness of sins, the resurrection of the body, and the life everlasting. Amen.
